subject: ENGLISH
title: Clap the Syllables · M01 D10
objective: Count spoken syllables in familiar words.
introduction: Clap with Milo! Ta-ble, win-dow, ba-na-na — how many beats do you hear?

vocabulary.definition: A part of a word with one vowel sound.
The letters a, e, i, o, u.
A sound is something you hear, like each beat you clap in a word.

activities.instruction: Watch how clapping helps you count the beats in a word!
activities.content: A syllable is a spoken beat with a vowel sound. Clapping helps hear beats but does not by itself determine spelling.

feedback.correct: Nice work. Continue to the next step.

items.prompt: How many beats do you hear in "table"?
items.explanation: Ta-ble has two beats: ta and ble. You say it with two claps, not one or four.

items.prompt: Which word has the right beat count?
items.explanation: Table is said ta-ble, so it has two beats. One beat and four beats do not match how we say the word.

items.prompt: Which way of counting syllables is WRONG?

options.text: Saying ba-na-na and clapping three times

items.explanation: Letters are not beats — table has 5 letters but only 2 beats. Clapping as you say each part of the word is the right way.

items.prompt: How many spoken beats are in banana?
items.explanation: Ba-na-na has three beats: ba, na, na. Say it slowly and clap — you will make three claps.

items.prompt: Which word has the right number of beats?
items.explanation: Ba-na-na has three beats, so the count is right. Counting letters or using spelling alone gives the wrong answer.
